page: Google Cloud Platform g2-standard-4 is a graphics-optimized virtual machine belonging to the g2 server family. It features a dedicated Intel Xeon x86_64 processor with 4 vCPUs (2 physical cores, 2 threads per core) running at 2.2 GHz, paired with 16.0 GB of system memory. The primary hardware accelerator is a single NVIDIA L4 GPU based on the Ada Lovelace architecture, equipped with 24 GB of VRAM. This instance does not include local storage or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data reveals a clear performance asymmetry between the host CPU and the GPU accelerator. Standard CPU-bound tasks, such as stress-ng multi-core tests, Geekbench single-core and multi-core scores, and Passmark CPU evaluations, consistently rank in the bottom 25% of tested servers. Memory bandwidth and decompression speeds are also relatively low. Conversely, the integrated NVIDIA L4 GPU delivers top-tier performance (top 10%) for large language model (LLM) inference, achieving 11,768.22 tokens/sec for prompt processing on small (135M) models and 52.18 tokens/sec for text generation on medium (7B) models.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the g2-standard-4 offers a specialized resource profile where budget is directed toward GPU acceleration rather than high-performance general-purpose compute. The modest CPU and memory allocation serve as a control plane for the GPU. This configuration is highly suited for GPU-accelerated workloads such as small-to-medium LLM inference, machine learning model serving, and graphics rendering, whereas it is poorly suited for CPU-heavy compilation, database operations, or high-throughput web serving.
